thesis: Galaxy Digital Inc. is a global digital-asset financial services and infrastructure company listed on Nasdaq (GLXY). **[Fact]** It serves institutional allocators, hedge funds, family offices, and qualified individuals through trading, investment banking, asset management, staking, tokenization, and custody technology. **[Fact]** Reportable segments are **Digital Assets**, **Data Centers** (Helios HPC campus in Texas), and **Treasury and Corporate** (proprietary digital-asset and venture investments). **[Fact]** The company went public via reorganization in 2025; FY2025 was its first full year as a U.S. registrant. **[Fact]** As of December 31, 2025, the platform had about **$12.3 billion** in assets and **190.7 million** Class A shares outstanding.
why_market_wrong: The stock may trade like a levered crypto proxy while understating the recurring fee and infrastructure franchise. **[Inference]** FY2025 **Adjusted EBITDA was only $33.7 million** (down from **$715.4 million** in 2024) because treasury marks and trading volatility dominated GAAP earnings, not because fee lines collapsed: **fees rose 54%** to **$159 million** and blockchain rewards grew to **$220 million**. **[Inference]** The **Helios** data-center pivot (CoreWeave lease, **133 MW** of critical IT load targeted by mid-2026) is priced as optionality with **zero Data Center segment revenue** in FY2025. **[Inference]** Complexity (dual share classes, digital-asset balance sheet, mark-to-market earnings) keeps generalist investors away, so the market may overweight trailing losses and underweight institutional wallet share.
